subject: KMS implementation readiness, key lineage summary & rotation logs — Foxline SIG request
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@foxline.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Auditor Team <audit@secureaudit.com>
Date: 2028-03-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG request — KMS key lineage & rotation

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As part of our SIG review the security team has asked for a concise package covering Redwood's KMS/HSM posture specific to the tenant that will host Foxline workloads. Can you provide the following?

- Key lineage mapping (logical key IDs/pseudonyms, creation and rotation timestamps, and whether a key is customer-managed or Redwood-managed)
- Rotation logs for the last 12 months (who initiated rotation, key version IDs, and sequence)
- HSM attestation or statement of configuration (modules used, FIPS level, multi‑party separation if applicable)
- Short note on in-transit and at-rest wrapping (KEK/DEK flow we use for tenant data)
- Confirmation of access control: which roles can export/unwrap keys, and where the KEK is stored/wrapped

We attached the SIG template; we don't need a full SOC artifact set for now — just the items above plus any small extracts or CSV logs you can share. Goal is to close the crypto items on our SIG checklist in the next two weeks.

Thanks — can you confirm ETA?

Warmly,
Tara Singh
Head of Vendor Security
Foxline Systems

Attachment: foxline_kms_requirements_v2.pdf (1 page checklist)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@foxline.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Auditor Team <audit@secureaudit.com>
Date: 2028-03-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG request — KMS key lineage & rotation

Tara — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned and can provide a compact package that maps to each of your bullets. Summary and plan below, attaching a short attestation and an initial log extract.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Key model: Tenant data keys are DEKs (per-tenant), wrapped with a KEK managed in an HSM-backed keystore. Foxline can opt for BYOK (customer-supplied KEK) or Redwood-managed KEK.
- HSM: We use FIPS-140-2 level 3 compliant modules with HSM tenancy isolation. Attestation stub attached.
- Rotation: Automated monthly rotations by default; ad-hoc rotations logged and tied to operator actions/CI jobs.

Deliverables we will provide by EOD 2028-03-12 (UTC):
1) Key lineage CSV (key_id, tenant_id, created_at, rotated_at[], current_version, manager_type) — rotation_logs_2027-06_to_2028-02.csv
2) HSM attestation summary (hsm_attestation_sig.txt)
3) Short explainer on in-transit wrapping and KEK placement (included in the attestation file and internal runbook excerpt)
4) Access matrix: roles that can request unwrap/export and the approval workflow (inline in this thread)

Action items: Priyom, can you assemble the rotation CSV and grep the operator audit events for the last 9 months? Laura — please confirm the attestation text is ready to sign.

Tara — if you prefer BYOK, let me know and we'll include the BYOK handshake notes for TOC. Otherwise we'll provide the standard Redwood-managed mapping.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-03-12T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG request — rotation logs and lineage (rotation_logs_2027-06_to_2028-02.csv)

Sergio/Team — attaching the requested rotation export and a short excerpt here. The CSV contains columns: key_alias, key_uuid, tenant_id, created_at, rotated_at, operator, rotation_reason, version_id. Sample rows (anonymized):

key_alias,key_uuid,tenant_id,created_at,rotated_at,operator,rotation_reason,version_id
tenant-dek-foxline,3f9a2c8b,foxline,2027-06-03T02:12:44Z,2027-12-01T03:05:09Z,ops-rotate-schedule,scheduled,v2
tenant-dek-foxline,3f9a2c8b,foxline,2027-12-01T03:05:09Z,2028-02-09T21:20:12Z,ci-triggered-rotate,security-review,v3

Notes on provenance and controls:
- Rotations are performed by our rotation service which emits signed events to the audit log; exports here are hashed and the HSM attestation includes the HSM-generated seal per rotation.
- KEK storage: KEKs are root-wrapped within the HSM key hierarchy and the KEK private material is non-exportable when Redwood-managed. For customers with BYOK, the external KEK is wrapped and stored, and we maintain the wrapping envelope and audit ties.
- Access control: only members of the CryptoOps role (least privilege group) along with an approver from Security can initiate manual unwrap/export flows; automated rotations are privileged CI workflows with restricted service accounts.

Attached: rotation_logs_2027-06_to_2028-02.csv

Let me know if the auditor needs the event IDs (we can redact IPs).

- Priyom
Principal Applied Cryptography Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@foxline.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Auditor Team <audit@secureaudit.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-13T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG request — KMS key lineage & rotation

Sergio / Priyom — this is great, thank you. The CSV and attestation cover most of what we need for the SIG review. A couple of follow-ups so we can mark this item closed:

- Can you provide a one-page signed attestation on Redwood letterhead stating: (a) the HSM model and FIPS level, (b) non-exportability of RED-managed KEKs, and (c) the canonical contact for emergency rotations? (This can be the hsm_attestation_sig.txt file if it includes a signature.)
- For the SIG evidence bundle we also need a concise mapping table we can paste into the questionnaire: Key alias -> Key UUID -> Current version -> Last rotation timestamp. The CSV is perfect but a 5-line extracted table would be ideal.
- Lastly, please confirm whether Foxline will be treated as BYOK if we deliver our KEK material, or Redwood-managed by default. We prefer BYOK but can accept Redwood-managed if the attestation and isolation meet our controls.

Proposed ETA for final items: 2028-03-15 EOD PT. Is that feasible? If so we'll schedule a final short review call.

Thanks again — Tara
Tara Singh
Head of Vendor Security
Foxline Systems
